title: The New York union's attitude compared with Chicago
summary: Hodes explains the six-month wait for a card and admires New York's local. He says Chicago's union later told him to ask first, while New York said to go ahead.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Now, whether that law was right or wrong, I don't know, that they put up that high tariff. And it's not only in New York. I have a great admiration for the local in New York. They're a very -- they see way out, they don't just see the view close up to the eye. Chicago, when I got back to

Chicago, they told me at the union, now, you've been to New York and we don't do things like New York or Los Angeles. So before you do anything, you come up here and ask. And the attitude in New York was, go ahead and do it. And if it's not right, we'll either catch you or we'll tell you. But they didn't say, don't do it.
